implementation_notes: interface declares the contract and the implementation can live in a different module; Kotlin adds interface delegation (class Derived(b: Base) : Base by b) so a class satisfies a contract by forwarding to a supplied object with no boilerplate, which is often the entire wiring story. Default methods let a published contract grow without breaking implementors, and the hand-written forwarding class remains right when the delegate must be adapted.
pitfalls: Members overridden in the delegating class are not seen by the delegate's own implementation, which calls its own methods.
JVM default methods depend on the -Xjvm-default mode; mixing modes can break binary compatibility with older compiled Kotlin code.
An interface property cannot have a backing field, so every implementation must supply the state itself.
